doc.title: Ray Sherman interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 13, 1998

title: Current listening: classical recordings and CD sound
summary: He enjoys Gerard Schwarz's CD sets and defends CD sound over LPs.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Listening to classical music, then and now

blocks.x: What do you listen to these days yourself?

You know I got a nice set, I subscribe to Gerard Schwarz, do you know that name? He’s conductor of the Seattle Symphony. He was originally a trumpet player, like a virtuoso, and he became a conductor, it must have been like 20 years ago. I remember seeing him

at the Pasadena, the small chamber orchestra. And now in Seattle he puts out this thing of a two CD package of like the basic repertoire of symphony orchestras, and each set is a different composer. So one CD is the music, and the other CD is like a lecture, with excerpts from the music and explaining the form and a little bit of the history of the guy’s life and the period, and it’s very good. And like you’re just listening to — I’d had most of the stuff on LP, you know the music, but people say they don’t like CDs, I don’t understand any of it. To me it’s so clear, no background noise.
Yeah. Some people miss, they say, the warmth.

Yeah. Of course people have different ears. Women I think I’ve heard, it’s strident. Of course women hear higher pitches than men. I can remember when transistor radios and stuff came out. I can kind of hear a little difference, then from the tube stuff, so it must be something like that. But what you’re getting though, I mean it doesn’t annoy me at all, and to hear it all, and especially the stereo, like I say if you hear all the individual instruments and the different sections, especially from a composer’s standpoint, to hear what the guy’s doing, nothing is covered up, you can hear everything. And maybe because he’s such a great musician, I mean he’s picking really good — they’re not all his performances, but whatever he picks to do are great performances. So just to sit down and listen, that’s kind of what I’ve been listening to. I don’t know, I shouldn’t get too critical.
